'''Mantsi''' (also known as '''Ma’as''' or '''Mangas''') is an endangered [[Afro-Asiatic languages|Afro-Asiatic]] language spoken in Mangas town in [[Bauchi State]], [[Nigeria]].<ref name=e18/> Blench (2020) reports that it is also called ''Mantsi''. According to Blench, the structure of Mantsi differs significantly from the other [[South Bauchi languages]].<ref name="Blench">Blench, Roger. 2020. ''[https://www.academia.edu/44200152/An_introduction_to_Mantsi_a_South_Bauchi_language_of_Central_Nigeria An introduction to Mantsi, a South Bauchi language of Central Nigeria]''.</ref>

Word lists of Mantsi had previously been published in Kiyoshi Shimizu's (1978) South Bauchi survey, which first mentioned the existence of the language.<ref>Shimizu, Kiyoshi 1978. ''The Southern Bauchi Group of Chadic Languages: A survey report''. Coll. Africana Marburgensia, n° 2 (Special Issue).</ref> An unpublished word list was also recorded by Ronald Cosper (n.d.).<ref>Cosper, Ronald n.d. Wordlist of South Bauchi (West Chadic) languages; Boghom, Mangas, Buli, Dott, Geji, Jimi, Polci, Sayanci, Zul. ms.</ref>

==Names==
Mantsi speakers refer to their language as ''Pyik Mantsi'' [pʲìk mántsì], and to themselves as the ''Mantsi'' [mántsì] people. Although there are fewer than 1,000 speakers, the language is still being spoken by children.<ref name="Blench"/>

==Demographics==
Mantsi is spoken in the single village of Mantsi (locally known as ''Maɗana'' [mánànā] or ''Ma’as'' [màʔās]) in the southern part of [[Bauchi (city)|Bauchi]] LGA, [[Bauchi State]]. The [[Kir language|Kir]] [Kyiir] and [[Balar language|Laar]] peoples, who speak closely related but distinct languages, live just to the northeast of Mantsi village in the nearby villages of Kir and Laar, respectively.<ref name="Blench"/>

==Classification==
Mantsi belongs to the Kir branch of the [[South Bauchi languages]]. It is most closely related to [[Kir language|Kir]] and [[Balar language|Laar]], as shown by the lexical comparisons below.<ref name="Blench"/>

==Phonology==
Mantsi has 3 level tones, as well as rising and falling contour tones.<ref name="Blench"/>

==Grammar==
Number is not marked morphologically.<ref name="Blench"/>
